steps.text: Put the base in DARK BLUE mode (power-button LED). Native PlayStation mode: short-press the power button until the LED is dark blue.
steps.source: GT DD Pro manual 5.6; Fanatec help

steps.text: Firmware: the current set is base 1.9.2.3 (Fanatec App 1.6.1.3, 2026-09-21). Updating needs a Windows PC with the base in RED mode; afterwards switch back, recalibrate the wheel centre and recheck your slot values.
Switch to the Advanced Tuning Menu: hold the Tuning button for about 4 s (Fanatec's FAQ says 3 s). The Standard menu cannot show: SETUP 4 SET, INT 4, FEI 90, FOR 90.
Do not use A SET for F1 25: it hands control to the game and locks the values, and F1 25 support for it is undocumented.
Give this driver their own spare slot (4 SET or 5 SET) with the lighter FF below, so switching drivers is one menu change.
Set SEN on the wheel to 360, the same as Maximum Wheel Rotation in the game. Do not rely on AUTO in F1 (known issue). Turn the wheel 90 degrees and check the on-screen wheel matches.
steps.source: Fanatec App 1.6.1.3 known issues; Fanatec F1 25 pages

steps.text: F1 25 v1.25 known bug: if the wheel oscillates or loses force feedback after a session change (for example Qualifying to Race), pause and power-cycle the base. Do not tune NDP, INT or the damper against it. Every report that states a torque is at 8 Nm.
Change one thing at a time, then drive the same car and track and run the rig check to compare.
steps.source: Fanatec F1 25 and oscillation pages; SimXPro (rig-setup-sources.md 7)

steps.text: MPS and AP are left out: the Bundled Gran Turismo DD Pro rim has no multi-position switch or analogue paddles. Skip them if the menu shows them. Not recommended here because it is not known whether the Bundled Gran Turismo DD Pro rim has them: SHO (vibration motors). If the menu shows them, leave them at their defaults.

sections.title: 4. Pedals: Fanatec CSL Pedals (stock, 2 or 3 pedals)

steps.text: After every power-on, press the throttle and brake fully once and release them before driving.
steps.source: Fanatec CSL Pedals product page, Explorer guide and Pedals FAQ
steps.detail: The CSL Pedals calibrate min/max automatically as they are pressed; until then the readings can be wrong.

steps.text: Nothing to set on the pedals: the stock brake measures travel with a 12-bit Hall sensor (not a potentiometer). There is no BRF and no manual calibration.
The pedals connect by RJ12 to the wheel base (the only path on a console).
After a session, open the rig check: brake input at rest, whether 100% throttle and brake are reached, how long the brake sits at 100% and whether the peaks drift during the session.

safety.text: Lighter wheel for this driver: FF 60 in their own slot, a peak of about 3.0 Nm instead of 5.0 Nm.
safety.detail: pitwall rule, no published source: a beginner or young driver gets a lighter wheel by scaling base FF in their own custom slot. Lower peak torque means a gentler wheel when the car spins or hits a kerb, and less fatigue. Base FF caps every force the base sends; the endstop does not depend on FF on current firmware. The default was set on the 5 Nm base: on a stronger base it shrinks by the ratio of the two tables' peak torques (60% becomes 40% at 8 Nm), so the Boost Kit does not make the wheel heavier. A force the driver sets on the slider is used as given.

safety.text: Keep thumbs on the front of the rim, not hooked behind the spokes: a direct-drive wheel can snap round when the car spins or hits a wall.

notes: Hall position brake: no BRF. Press-fully routine after power-on.
warnings: No published source for Comfort here: No source: derived by pitwall. Built from Fanatec guidance (FOR 80-90 for fatigue, FEI 80-90 if harsh, NDP as the calming tool) and low canned effects to cut noise.

rules.rule: For comfort, scale VIB_FFB_STRENGTH by 5/8 (about x0.63) to keep the 5 Nm weight, then adjust by feel.

For an exact A/B against the old 5 Nm feel, set FF 63 at 8 Nm with unchanged in-game values; this reproduces the 5 Nm torque map, including its clipping. Endstop strength does not depend on FF on current firmware.

Base FW >= 1.9.0.2 raised Boost Kit holding torque from 6 to 8 Nm, so long high-load corners feel heavier than 8 Nm presets made on older firmware. If the first sessions are tiring, lower in-game strength in steps of 5-10 or use the comfort entry.
With the Boost Kit on base FW >= 1.9.0.2 FFS is not offered (Fanatec App 1.5.1.2 changelog). Set FFS PEA only if the menu still shows it (LIN gives ~6 Nm).

Hands-off oscillation on straights: raise NDP in steps of 5 first, keep INT 1-5, then lower strength, then a little NFR; NIN with care (Fanatec oscillation guide). With NDP OFF at 8 Nm expect to need NDP 5-20 [U]. Oscillation starting at a session boundary in F1 25 v1.25+ is a known game bug, not a settings fault.

known_issues.title: F1 25 v1.25: the wheel oscillates or loses FFB after a session change
known_issues.detail: Since v1.25 (2026-09-07) CSL DD / GT DD Pro owners report violent left-right oscillation or lost FFB after a session change or restart (for example Qualifying to Race), until the base is power-cycled. Pause and power-cycle the base; do not tune NDP, INT or the damper against it (it happened at NDP 50 / INT 11, and FUL OFF did not help). Every report that states a torque is at 8 Nm, and no PS5 report was found. EA confirmed it and shared a fix with Fanatec on 2026-10-07 (no ETA). The rig check flags it as 'Oscillation after a session change'.
known_issues.source: EA forums threads 13695137, 13701405, 13701710; forum.fanatec.com topic 20597 (PS5 impact unverified)

known_issues.title: F1 25 v1.25: FFB reported lighter
known_issues.detail: Players on several brands report lighter or less detailed FFB after v1.25, so values from before September may feel lighter. Carson raised his 8 Nm strength by 10-20. Start at the upper end of a published range and adjust by feel.

known_issues.title: FullForce weaker than intended on CSL DD / GT DD Pro
known_issues.detail: Fanatec App 1.6.1.3 known issue. No source shows that F1 25 implements FullForce: leave FUL at its default for F1.

known_issues.title: SEN AUTO misbehaves in F1 games
known_issues.detail: Fanatec App 1.6.1.3 known issue (seen on PC). Set SEN by hand to the in-game rotation.

known_issues.title: The Fanatec mobile app does not work with the new Windows App
known_issues.detail: Its own release notes say so. There is no console path for base settings on PS5 other than the on-wheel Tuning Menu.
known_issues.source: Fanatec App 1.6.1.3 release notes; App Store listing

known_issues.title: F1 25: a small FFB bump when Straight Mode switches
known_issues.detail: Reported by a DD+ owner on PS5 Pro. Not a fault; the rig check ignores it.

known_issues.title: F1 25: FFB dropping mid-race on PS5
known_issues.detail: Community reports; toggling Vibration & Force Feedback restored it.

upcoming.label: Boost Kit 180 (8 Nm)

steps.text: Fit the Boost Kit 180 in place of the standard PSU. The base detects it and releases 8 Nm automatically; there is no setup step.
steps.source: Fanatec help 30312080999825; GT DD Pro manual 5.6.4

steps.text: Check FFS on your base: it is not offered with the Boost Kit on base firmware 1.9.0.2 or later. If it is still shown, set PEA (LIN caps the base at about 6 Nm). Note what each slot reports as maximum torque.
steps.source: Fanatec App 1.5.1.2 release notes; slot report GTPlanet 2026-09-12 (unverified)

steps.text: The endstop does not depend on FF on current firmware, so a lower FF never weakens it.
Vibration & Force Feedback Strength is lowered from 60 to 40 (60 x 5/8, pitwall derived, to keep the 5 Nm weight).

Holding torque is now 8 Nm (firmware 1.9.0.2 or later), so long high-load corners feel heavier than on older-firmware 8 Nm presets. If the first sessions are tiring, step Vibration & Force Feedback Strength down by 5-10.
Expect more hands-off oscillation at 8 Nm. With NDP OFF you may need NDP 5-20: raise it in steps of 5 and compare the rig check before and after.
steps.source: viewer comments on Fin's 8 Nm video; Fanatec oscillation guide

steps.text: F1 25 v1.25: if the wheel oscillates or loses FFB after a session change, pause and power-cycle the base. Every report that states a torque is at 8 Nm. Do not tune against it.
Keep airflow around the base (it is passively cooled). Fanatec publishes no thermal data for the GT DD Pro at 8 Nm.

notes: Peak wheel torque: about 3.0 Nm now, 4.8 Nm with the kit; Vibration & Force Feedback Strength drops from 60 to 40 to keep about the same weight.

diffs.label: Brake Force (set in the wheel base Tuning Menu)

steps.text: Update the base firmware before installing the kit (Windows PC, Fanatec App, base in RED mode). Then back to DARK BLUE, recalibrate the wheel centre and recheck your slots.
steps.source: Fanatec Load Cell Kit manual; App 1.6.1.3 notes

steps.text: Wiring: RJ12 from the accelerator's 'Wheel Base / Load Cell' port to the load cell's 'Load Cell' port, accelerator to the base. Never connect RJ12 and USB at the same time.
steps.source: Fanatec CSL Pedals Load Cell Kit manual

steps.text: Set BRF in the Tuning Menu (it appears in the Standard menu too once the load cell is detected). Start at the value in the wheel table.

Owners of this exact kit (CSL Pedals Load Cell Kit, stock, latest value each, n=5) run BRF 30, 40, 55, 70, 90: median 55. pitwall's starting points by style are derived from them: Official 050 (factory default), Balanced 055 (050-060), Competitive 070 (065-075), Realism 065 (065-075), Comfort 040 (035-045).

Tune BRF so a firm press you can repeat every lap reaches 100%, not your maximum effort. Do 10 identical stops: if the peaks vary a lot, lower BRF; if 100% comes too easily (long plateaus at 100% in the rig check), raise it.
steps.source: EveZone and SimXPro load-cell guides (community method)
steps.detail: Roughly 70-80% of your physical limit; reaching 100% should not need straining or lifting off the seat. A light stand or Playseat forces a lower BRF.

steps.text: After every power-on, press each pedal fully once (hold the brake at maximum for 2-3 s) and release. There is no manual calibration without a PC.
steps.source: Fanatec Pedals FAQ; community note on the hold

steps.text: Locking too easily? Raise BRF, lower Brake Pressure in the F1 25 car setup, or add brake linearity. BLI is not available (it needs ClubSport V3 pedals).
steps.source: Fanatec Tuning Menu article; Trophi/Driver61 braking guides

steps.text: These are hardware faults, not reasons to change BRF: the peak suddenly far below 100% at your usual press, the signal oscillating under constant pressure, a light press reading full brake, or input with your foot off the pedal. Recheck BRF on the wheel, update firmware, then contact support.
Manual min/max calibration needs a Windows PC and is reset by a load-cell firmware update. If the brake reads input at rest, Fanatec's fix is a firmware update plus a pedal reset via PC.
The old CSL brake can be refitted as a clutch; F1 25 and GT7 do not need one.
Run the rig check after fitting and compare it with a session from before the upgrade.
